transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-20 14:30 UTC
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Lena (ForestFall SRE), Daniel (VP Eng), Aisha (CTO), Tom (oncall), Priya (Product)

Summary:
- Follow-up on the 2026-05-12 long tail latency surge impacting interactive chat sessions. Align on short-term fallbacks, runbook updates and scope a 2-week resilience sprint to harden KV cache, autoscaling, and circuit breakers. Plan a bench test that mirrors ForestFall's mixed small-chat + embedding workload.

Topics:
- Root-cause hypotheses (KV cache miss storms, cold KV partitions, priority routing imbalance)
- Short-term mitigations: prefix caching, emergency fallback model, throttling at edge, autoscale policy adjustments
- Long-term hardenings: pinning critical endpoints to dedicated capacity, improved observability (token-level traces), and runbook automation for fallback rollouts

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick check - is this still a good time?
[00:05] Lena (ForestFall): yeah good here, we're a bit stretched but we pushed folks into this slot.
[00:09] Arjun (Redwood SE): cool, we'll try to keep it focused. we reviewed your postmortem draft last night, thanks for that btw, it helped.
[00:15] Daniel (ForestFall): thanks — we want to be practical: symptoms were p99 spikes and long tails during peak traffic between 10–12 PDT. Some customers saw timeouts then retry storms.
[00:25] Tom (Oncall): to add, our oncall saw KV cache eviction rates spike, and that seemed to correlate with downstream retries into the hosted route.
[00:33] Arjun (Redwood SE): right, our preliminary telemetry also shows hot spots in a small subset of keys — could be a shard imbalance or eviction churn. we called out two plausible paths: one is that your prefix caching wasn't applied for some streaming endpoints, second is that prewarm/autoscale ramp didn't trigger quickly enough.
[00:48] Lena: hmm when you say prefix caching—are you talking about the redis-esque layer or the Redwood prefix/kvcache? sometimes our names get mixed in notes.
[00:55] Maya: yeah sorry, Redwood prefix KV (we call it KV cache) — we saw low hit rates for long prompt chains, so the system was regenerating context more often.
[01:03] Aisha (CTO): we also noticed a CPU spike on the orchestration nodes when many small requests hit in parallel, that pushed autoscaler thresholds.
[01:12] Arjun: that matches; small short-request patterns can cause higher per-token overhead if batching isn't effective. so what we want to do: immediate mitigations to stop user-visible timeouts, and then run a resilience sprint to remove the root causes.
[01:22] Daniel: what are immediate things we can flip without risk?
[01:25] Maya: three low-risk toggles: 1) emergency fallback model (slower but cheaper) for timed-out requests, 2) enable conservative circuit-breaker throttling at the API gateway so retries don't amplify, 3) temporarily pin the most critical endpoints to dedicated capacity during business hours.
[01:38] Tom: pinning needs procurement sign-off for dedicated — but we can do a short demo of capacity reservation.
[01:44] Sofia (CSM): we can set a trial for the pinning for 48 hours, Redwood will instrument and roll back automatically.
[01:50] Lena: on the circuit-breaker—what thresholds do you recommend?
[01:53] Arjun: start with p99 latency window: if p99 exceeds 800ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows, trip the breaker and route to fallback model; also apply a token-rate throttle per token-per-minute per org to slow retries. these are conservative to avoid false trips.
[02:10] Daniel: 800ms seems high for us; our internal SLA is 300ms p99. is there a way to do tiered fallbacks so premium customers don't see fallback?
[02:18] Maya: yes — policy routing by tier is supported. we can mark premium endpoints to always attempt dedicated first and apply a higher trip threshold.
[02:24] Priya (Product): quick q — how intrusive are these changes? we need to know rollback steps.
[02:28] Arjun: all changes are feature-flagged. we'll push a runbook PR and test in staging. rollback is one button to revert the policy and restore previous routing. we'll also add a canary for 5% of traffic first.
[02:40] Lena: we're worried about correctness regression with fallback model — sometimes it hallucinate on structured outputs.
[02:45] Maya: totally valid. fallback model will be used only on timeouts; we'll keep it in inference-only mode and ensure structured output schema validation is applied post-response. Also we'll add automatic quality filters — if the fallback fails schema checks, return an error rather than a low-quality response.
[02:59] Aisha: ok that helps. what about the root cause—cache eviction and shard hotness?
[03:04] Arjun: on the cache side, we propose two workstreams: A) tune eviction policy + increase prewarm on hot keys; B) add adaptive prefix caching that extends TTLs for keys with high access bursts. For shard hotness, we can reshard / rebalance but that's a heavier operation — we'll simulate in bench tests first.
[03:24] Daniel: bench test — what would you like from our side?
[03:27] Arjun: a replayable traffic capture (p99 traces + request shapes) for the surge window. if you can supply a 10–20 minute sample that mimics the mix (small chat 70%, embedding 20%, long-form 10%), we'll run a 2-hour bench at scale.
[03:40] Lena: we can pull that. Tom will send the logs.
[03:43] Tom: yes I'll anonymize and send S3 link.
[03:46] Sofia: Redwood will also share a runbook diff showing suggested circuit breaker thresholds, route policy, and the quick rollback steps.
[03:52] Maya: on observability, we propose adding token-level tracing for the next 7 days to catch p999 escalations — it'll add minimal overhead and will be rotated out after the bench.
[04:02] Daniel: curious — do you use any dynamic kernel selection that might change performance characteristics during long prompts?
[04:07] Arjun: yup we have compilation/kernel heuristics — sometimes for long sequences the runtime picks a different kernel path that is more memory efficient but slightly slower per token. that can interact with batching and cause odd latency shapes. we flagged that in the postmortem and will force a consistent kernel for the bench.
[04:21] Priya: what about compliance artifacts — teams want assurance on data residency and KMS usage for the bench.
[04:27] Sofia: we'll share our KMS & SOC2 docs. bench can run in your VPC/test region if you need.
[04:33] Aisha: the bench in our VPC is preferred, if possible. less network variance.
[04:37] Maya: we can run the bench in your VPC with a short-lived agent; we'll provide exact setup steps.
[04:42] Lena: ok, timeline — what are the sprint goals?
[04:45] Arjun: two-week sprint: week 1 — immediate toggles, runbook PR, bench setup; week 2 — bench runs, iterate on cache TTLs, and pilot pinning for priority endpoints. deliverable: a validated runbook and a pilot contract for dedicated capacity for critical endpoints.
[05:00] Daniel: is there a cost estimate for pinning? rough ballpark to discuss with finance.
[05:05] Maya: for a 48-hour pilot it's minimal — we can give a rough number once you list the endpoints and expected QPS. for monthly commit, we'll follow the Dedicated pricing page but give you a pilot discount.
[05:15] Tom: what about alerting thresholds — we had late detection during the last incident.
[05:19] Arjun: add synthetic probes at 15s intervals for the critical endpoints and a separate SLA monitor that tracks tail latency separately (p99/p999) and fires earlier than aggregate 5m windows. we'll share recommended Grafana alerts.
[05:33] Lena: action items summary?
[05:35] Sofia: I'll capture: Redwood runbook diff (Arjun), bench schedule (Maya+ForestFall), p99 trace export (Lena), SOC2/KMS docs (Sofia), pilot endpoint list (Daniel).
[05:45] Maya: thanks — last thing, are there any blockers on the ForestFall side we should know about?
[05:48] Daniel: procurement needs a 3-day lead for any dedicated capacity trial, and security needs to vet the bench agent (we'll provide the contact).
[05:55] Maya: understood, we'll align on contacts in the next 24 hours.
[05:59] Aisha: thanks everyone, appreciate the practical plan.
[06:02] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the runbook PR and schedule the bench.

Meeting close.

Notes on transcription quality and artifacts: occasional speaker mislabels (oncall vs SRE) and a few product name swaps (prefix KV vs Redis) — corrected in summary. References: linked artifacts mentioned in chat: "postmortem-draft.md" (ForestFall private link), "bench-spec.xlsx" (Redwood shared sheet), SOC2 & KMS integrations (Redwood.sec/docs link).
